entities.name: Adriano Bernareggi
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Adriano Bernareggi (1884–1953) was an Italian Catholic bishop who served as Bishop of Bergamo from 1932 to 1953 — an episcopate that coincided with the Fascist period, the Second World War, and the early post-war reconstruction of Italian society and Church life. Born in the Brianza region of Lombardy, he was deeply formed by the Ambrosian theological tradition and by the social Catholicism of the early twentieth century.

His episcopate at Bergamo is particularly significant in the light of that diocese's later history: Bergamo was the home diocese of Angelo Roncalli (the future Pope John XXIII) and subsequently of Pope John Paul I. Bernareggi's governance of the diocese created the pastoral environment in which a generation of Bergamasque clergy were formed, contributing to the broader renewal that would characterise Italian Catholicism in the post-war period.

Bernareggi's management of the diocese during the Fascist period and the war required navigating the complex relationship between the Church and Mussolini's regime — a relationship formally defined by the Lateran Accords of 1929 but constantly tested by the regime's ambitions and the Church's pastoral concerns. His post-war reconstruction work at Bergamo contributed to Italian Catholic Action's rebuilding of civil society in northern Italy.
